species_support: mouse bleomycin-induced pulmonary-fibrosis model and primary lung fibroblast assays
evidence_summary: Primary studies show direct CXCL10-syndecan-4 interaction by radioligand binding and chemical crosslinking, with syndecan-4-dependent inhibition of fibroblast migration and antifibrotic activity; mutation of the CXCL10 heparin-binding domain reduces the effect.
limitations: Represent CXCL10-SDC4 as a heparan-sulfate proteoglycan interaction in the lung fibroblast/fibrosis context, distinct from CXCL10-CXCR3 signaling; do not infer a universal intracellular or terminal-TF route.

species_support: human systematic beta-arrestin screening of 43 chemokines against ACKR4
evidence_summary: A systematic primary screening study specifically disproved agonist activity of CXCL13 toward ACKR4 while confirming CCL19, CCL20, CCL21, CCL25 and partial CCL22 activity; the public CXCL13-ACKR4 row should not be materialized.
limitations: Represent CXCL13 with its supported receptor context and preserve the negative ACKR4 screen; do not infer ACKR4 binding from the earlier family-level annotation or from CXCL13 homology.

species_support: human CCL24/eotaxin-2 cloning, CCR3-transfected-cell binding and eosinophil chemotaxis assays
evidence_summary: Primary cloning and receptor assays identify CCL24/eotaxin-2 as a CCR3 ligand with eosinophil chemotactic activity; the cited study does not support transfer of the CCL24 pair to CCR2.
limitations: Represent CCL24-CCR3 with the tested eosinophil and receptor-transfectant context; do not transfer CCL11/CCL24 family evidence to CCR2 or infer a direct CCL24-CCR2 edge.

species_support: human/mouse atypical-chemokine-receptor ligand panels and CCX-CKR/ACKR4 binding and beta-arrestin assays
evidence_summary: Primary atypical-receptor studies place CCL21 in the homeostatic CCX-CKR/ACKR4 ligand context and define D6/ACKR2 around inflammatory chemokine recognition, but the current evidence does not isolate a direct CCL21-to-ACKR2 experiment.
limitations: Retain CCL21B-ACKR2 only as a receptor-family/context boundary with species and chemokine-processing limits; do not materialize a direct ACKR2 edge or transfer CCX-CKR/ACKR4 evidence to ACKR2.
